name: msgop
synopsis: int msgsnd(int msqid, const void *msgp, size_t msgsz, int msgflg);
ssize_t msgrcv(int msqid, void *msgp, size_t msgsz, long msgtyp, int msgflg);
description: The msgsnd() system call sends a message to a System V message queue, while msgrcv() receives a message from it. Both require the calling process to have appropriate permissions on the queue.

parameters.name: msgp
parameters.type: const void * (for msgsnd) or void * (for msgrcv)
parameters.description: Pointer to a caller-defined structure containing the message type and data

parameters.name: msgsz
parameters.description: Size of the message data in bytes

parameters.name: msgflg
parameters.description: Flags that modify the behavior, such as IPC_NOWAIT

parameters.name: msgtyp
parameters.description: Message type for selection in msgrcv(), must be greater than 0

return_value.success: msgsnd() returns 0; msgrcv() returns the number of bytes actually copied into the message buffer
return_value.failure: Both return -1 and set errno to indicate the error

errors.description: The calling process does not have the required permissions on the message queue
The message cannot be sent due to queue limits and IPC_NOWAIT was specified
The address pointed to by msgp is not accessible
The call was interrupted by a signal
Invalid argument, such as invalid msqid, msgsz, or mtype
Insufficient memory to copy the message
Message text length exceeds msgsz and MSG_NOERROR is not specified (for msgrcv)
No message of the requested type exists and IPC_NOWAIT was specified (for msgrcv)
Kernel not configured for certain flags (for msgrcv)

bugs: In Linux 3.13 and earlier, msgrcv() with MSG_COPY but without IPC_NOWAIT could return incorrect messages; specifying both MSG_COPY and MSG_EXCEPT was not diagnosed as an error until Linux 3.14.
versions: Linux-specific, with bug fixes in Linux 3.14
